newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Central sees gain from stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Central sees gain from stake sale.

text.p: Illinois Central Corp said Tuesday it has sold its investment in an insurance company which will result in a one-time, pre-tax gain in the fourth quarter of about $7 million which will be reflected in "other income" and will increase fourth quarter earnings by about $0.07 a share.

Earlier today, the company reported 1996 third quarter earnings rose to $32.1 million or $0.52 a share from $29.2 million or $0.47 in the year ago period. Third quarter 1996 revenues were $167.9 million, up 4.1 percent compared to $161.3 million for 1995.

Third quarter 1996 operating expenses of $106.4 million were down 1.7 percent resulting in an operating ratio of 63.4 percent, a 3.7 percentage-point improvement compared to third quarter 1995. Operating income for the 1996 third quarter of $61.5 million improved 15.8 percent compared to $53.1 million in third quarter 1995.

On June 13, 1996, Illinois Central acquired CCP Holdings Inc, parent of Chicago, Central & Pacific and Cedar River railroads. In the third quarter, CCP contributed $17 million in revenue, $4 million in operating income, and $2 million or $0.03 a share to net income.

Excluding CCP, third quarter revenues fell 6.5 percent on 16.8 percent fewer ton-miles. Gains in coal, chemicals, intermodal, and metals only partially offset weaknesses in other commodities, primarily grain, the railroad company said.

Illinois Central's grain ton-miles were down 72 percent for the quarter. Last year's smaller-than-normal corn harvest resulted in less product to transport in 1996, with inventories essentially exhausted in the third quarter, in advance of the October harvest, the company said.
